Control Room Operator.

Manx Automobile Assistance – Isle of Man.
Stoney Mountain Road, Foxdale.

** Full-Time or Part-Time **

Manx Automobile Assistance is a trusted vehicle recovery and roadside assistance provider serving customers across the Isle of Man. We pride ourselves on delivering a professional, reliable, and customer-focused service 24 hours a day.

We are looking for a calm, organised, and proactive Control Room Operator to join our growing team. You will be the first point of contact for customers requiring roadside assistance and recovery services, ensuring that help is dispatched quickly, efficiently, and professionally.

The Role:

As a Control Room Operator, you will play a vital role in coordinating our roadside assistance and recovery operations. You will manage incoming calls, liaise with customers and recovery technicians, dispatch the appropriate resources, and monitor jobs through to completion.
This position requires excellent communication skills, strong decision-making abilities, and the confidence to remain calm under pressure while managing multiple tasks simultaneously.

Key Responsibilities:

Answer and manage incoming calls from customers requiring roadside assistance and vehicle recovery.
Coordinate and dispatch recovery operators and technicians to incidents across the Isle of Man.
Monitor the progress of active jobs and provide updates to customers where required.
Ensure accurate recording of all customer and job information.
Maintain detailed logs and operational records.
Communicate effectively with drivers, technicians, customers, and business partners.
Prioritise workload and respond quickly to changing situations.
Support the smooth day-to-day running of the control room.
Assist with general administration duties including filing, invoicing, and data entry.
Contribute to continuous improvements within the business and support new operational processes when required.

What We're Looking For -

Essential Skills & Qualities:
Excellent customer service and communication skills.
Ability to remain calm and professional in high-pressure situations.
Strong organisational and multitasking abilities.
Good problem-solving and decision-making skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Competent computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
A proactive and flexible approach to work.

What We Offer:

Monday to Friday working pattern.
Competitive salary based on experience.
32 days holiday per year.
Full training provided.
Supportive and friendly working environment.
Opportunity to be part of a growing Isle of Man business with an excellent reputation.

To apply, please send your CV and a covering letter to – Timcole@manxaa.com

Our client seeks a Head of Compliance to join their team. Role Profile: To lead the execution of Compliance Risk Management processes and activities to ensure that the area is undertaken in a compliant manner to avoid operational losses, fines, penalties or reputational damage to the organisation and enable the competitive advantage of the organisation. Key Responsibilities: Analyse the operational activities within the Branch to identify compliance risks and therefore ensure adherence to the relevant Group compliance frameworks and standards. Build and maintain effective relationships with the country regulators and stakeholders on all areas of responsibility. Develop, track and report on the progress of the compliance monitoring plans for the IOM Branch in order to identify significant compliance breaches, exposures and potential areas of improvement. Drive customisation and maintain generic risk management plans (RMPs) to ensure it is appropriate within the regulatory context of the specific country. Guide the adherence to the data model across the compliance team to ensure the collection, capturing and management of data adheres to the required data standards and policies. Key Skills and Experience: First Degree in Audit. First Degree in Legal. First Degree in Risk Management. 3 - 4 years experience in Business Enablement. Experience and a solid understanding of the relevant banking environment including the associated products and activities specific to area in which this role is responsible. 8-10 years experience - The role requires a seasoned expert in Compliance with a sound knowledge of the relevant regulatory requirements and upcoming developments applicable to a specific business area as well as a solid understanding of banking products and activities. To drive an effectively compliant function, an influential leader is required with a proven track record in leading a Functional team of Compliance resources. Technical Competencies: Evaluation of Internal Control. sFinancial Acumen. Financial Industry Regulatory Framework. Legal Compliance. Process Governance. Risk Awareness. 
 If you have the required skills please apply online at searchandselect.com quoting reference number: 16614

To ensure testing criteria remains consistent with updated systems and controls and remains effectiveWorking with the business to strengthen its compliance culture by being approachable and clearly articulating requirements. To provide demonstrable support for the strategy of the Isle of Man business and the wider Group. Key Skills and Experience: The post-holder must have appropriate professional compliance qualifications or significant experience in a compliance role. Prior experience in developing and delivering a Compliance Monitoring Plan (CMP). Strong knowledge of the Isle of Man regulatory framework and international compliance standards. Experience within the TCSP sector (preferred but not essential). Ability to adapt to regulatory changes and implement best practices effectively. Strong report writing skills. Personal Attribute: Excellent organisational skills; Great inter-personal skills to communicate CMP Findings with the business lines and confidently discuss the way in which issues can be resolved; Ability to build and develop strong working relationships at all levels; High level of self-motivation and discipline.

Our client seeks an experienced Group Compliance Officer to join their team and take senior compliance and financial crime accountability across the group's regulated entities. Subject to regulatory approval, this is a hands-on, senior position with direct ownership of the regulatory relationship with both the UK FCA and the IOM FSA, and a defining role in shaping the group's compliance framework as their fund platform widens. Key Responsibilities: Discharge statutory Compliance Officer role under Part 9 of the IOM Financial Services Rule Book. Maintain compliance monitoring programmes, regulatory returns, and statutory registers. Oversee SMF16 Compliance Oversight function, with ownership of AIFMD, MIFIDPRU, MAR, SYSC, and COBS compliance. Lead FCA supervisory dialogue, regulatory returns and notifications including AIFMD Annex IV reports. Hold MLRO function, managing group sanctions screening and customer due diligence. Run group AML/CFT programmes with particular attention to maritime risk factors. Provide regulatory advice on existing and new fund vehicles across multiple jurisdictions. Embed strong compliance culture across London, Isle of Man, Cyprus and Geneva operations. Report to relevant boards and committees on compliance and financial crime risk matters. Key Skills and Experience: Minimum three years compliance experience in regulated financial services. Working knowledge of IOM Financial Services Rule Book and AML/CFT Code 2019. Recognised compliance qualification such as ICA Diploma in Compliance or CISI Diploma in Investment Compliance. Strong working knowledge of FCA rules relevant to full-scope AIFMs including AIFMD, MIFIDPRU, MAR, SYSC, COBS. Direct prior experience as MLRO at a corporate service provider or comparable regulated entity would be desirable. maritime, shipping or commodities sector experience would be ideal. Evidence of ability to satisfy FCA fitness and propriety standards for SMF16 approval.
 If you have the required skills please apply online at searchandselect.com quoting reference number: 16553

Port Erin Commissioners is seeking an experienced and highly motivated Clerk, the authority’s most senior officer, to provide strategic leadership and robust governance support to elected members and employees.  The postholder will play a central role in shaping and delivering the Authority’s priorities, ensuring high standards, compliance and accountability. 
 
The role includes close engagement with elected members, oversight of governance and decision-making processes and ensuring that the authority operates as an effective and efficient service provider to the community.  The postholder may also hold responsibility for information governance and complaints functions, subject to statutory requirements and the authority’s governance arrangements.
 
If you are ready for a new and exciting challenge, are committed to good governance and integrity, and want to deliver high quality services, while providing values driven leadership within a close knit community in Port Erin, then we want to hear from you.

We are establishing a new conveyancing practice in the Isle of Man and are looking for an experienced Senior Conveyancing Administrator to join us at an early stage and play a key role in shaping how the business operates from the ground up.
This is a rare opportunity to be involved not just in day-to-day case management, but in building processes, systems, and standards for a modern, efficient conveyancing service.
About the Role:
You will bring strong hands-on experience of residential conveyancing on the Isle of Man, with a practical understanding of both purchases and sales, and how transactions are progressed locally from instruction through to completion.
Working closely with the founders, you will:
Manage conveyancing files from start to finish (sales and purchases).
Help design and implement efficient workflows and processes.
Support the set-up of systems, templates, and client procedures.
Act as a key operational point of knowledge within the business.
What We’re Looking For:
Proven experience in Isle of Man conveyancing (essential).
Strong administrative and organisational skills at a senior level.
Practical knowledge of the full conveyancing lifecycle (pre-contract to completion and post-completion).
Ability to work independently and take initiative in a start-up environment.
A pragmatic, solutions-focused approach.
What We Offer:
The opportunity to get involved at the outset of a new and growing practice.
A genuine chance to shape how the business operates.
A supportive and collaborative working environment.
Competitive remuneration, dependent on experience.
________________________________________
If you are an experienced conveyancing professional looking for something more than a traditional role—and want to be part of building something from scratch—we would welcome a conversation.

For more details and to apply contact anthony@knightconsultancy.co

Our client seeks a Head of Compliance to join their team for a short contract. Full time or Part Time hours would be considered. This is a critical role which includes overseeing compliance monitoring, policy development, regulatory reporting, risk management (across financial, legal, regulatory, and operational domains), and acting as a key liaison with the IOMFSA and other stakeholders. Key Responsibilities: Act as the R13 Head of Compliance Controlled Function holder, fulfilling all associated responsibilities and maintaining fitness and propriety. Oversee compliance with all conditions of the licence and applicable Isle of Man regulatory requirements. Establish, maintain, and oversee robust, documented arrangements (policies, procedures, systems, and controls) appropriate to the nature, scale, and complexity of the business (Class 8(2a) & (4)) for compliance with all regulatory requirements. Ensure appropriate segregation of duties, safeguarding of client assets (including relevant funds under Class 8 rules), maintenance of records, and fair treatment of clients. Key Skills and Experience: Minimum 5 years of compliance experience within the financial services sector, with experience in a senior compliance role. Bachelor's degree in Law, Finance, Business, or a related field. Relevant professional compliance qualifications (e.g., ICA Diploma) are highly advantageous. For a full list of responsibilities and requirements or to apply for this great role, please visit the website at searchandselect.com, quoting the reference number: 16571

Notes
Altenar is a leading IT company founded in 2011 and headquartered in the Isle of Man, with offices in Malta, Greece, Georgia, Brazil and Uruguay.
We are seeking a proactive and detail oriented Junior Legal/Contracts Officer to support the legal, contracts, and governance functions of the business.
Key Responsibilities:
Assisting with the corporate governance of the Altenar group of Companies, including arranging board meetings and preparing agendas and board packs.
Assisting with the creation and preparation of documents for presentation to the Board of Directors for review and signature, particularly customer onboarding documentation.
Attending board meetings to assist with the recording and preparation of accurate board minutes.
Working with the Contracts Manager to ensure legal documents progress efficiently from drafting and collaboration (with all relevant stakeholders) through negotiation to  execution.
Ensuring physical and electronic filing is completed promptly and accurately, including  maintaining internal document databases and records.
Assisting the Compliance department with customer and supplier on-boarding processes.
Supporting general company administration, including insurance and data protection renewals and other corporate administrative requirements as they  arise. 
Assisting with banking administration and payment processes, as required.
Providing general administrative and ad-hoc business support as required from time to time.

Essential Requirements:
Good standard of general education, including GCSEs (or equivalent) in English and Maths.
Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and competing priorities.
Strong written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and professionalism.
Proactive and self motivated approach, with the ability to work independently and take ownership of tasks.
Willingness and aptitude to learn new processes, systems, and areas of the business.
Ability to follow instruction carefully while also using initiative and sound judgement

Desirable Requirements:
Previous experience in an administrative, governance, legal support, compliance or company secretarial role, including exposure to board meetings or governance processes
Experience working within a regulated industry or professional services environment.
Familiarity with legal documentation, contracts administration, or compliance processes.
Experience maintaining document management systems or internal databases.
Understanding of customer and supplier onboarding processes.
Knowledge of data protection requirements and general corporate administration.

For more details and to apply contact job@altenar.com

An awareness of Financial Services and associated legislation, regulation and guidance including trends and developments. Strong analytical skills, ability to quickly and accurately assimilate information, to consider any associated risks and to summarise the information effectively. Ability to work under pressure, manage a workload of varied complexity, to manage competing priorities and to deliver against deadlines. Notes
Our client seeks a commercially minded Legal Counsel to join their in-house team. Role Profile: This role offers the opportunity to take ownership of legal matters, work closely with the business, and play a hands-on role in shaping how legal supports a growing international company. This position is suited to a proactive and detail-oriented lawyer who is comfortable working independently, taking accountability, and driving continuous improvement in legal processes and documentation. Key responsibilities: Draft, review, and negotiate a wide range of commercial agreements, including SaaS/software licensing, partnerships, and supplier contracts. Act as a key legal contact for business stakeholders, providing clear, pragmatic, and commercially focused advice. Take ownership of legal support for designated business areas. Identify and implement improvements to legal processes, workflows, and ways of working. Develop and maintain contract templates, playbooks, and internal guidance. Collaborate with a multi-jurisdictional legal team. Manage external counsel and support disputes where required. Monitor relevant legal and regulatory developments in the gaming and technology sectors. Support strategic business initiatives, including new product development. Key Skills & Experience: 4-6 years PQE (post qualification experience) as a solicitor, advocate or equivalent required - this is a guideline so if you feel that you are suitable, please still apply. Strong grounding in commercial and contract law. Experience in the gaming industry/software development industry is advantageous but not essential. Ability to work independently, take ownership, and manage priorities. Experience improving legal processes, templates, or ways of working is highly desirable. Excellent drafting, negotiation, and communication skills. Ability to provide practical, business-focused advice in a clear and concise manner. Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to work effectively across different jurisdictions and cultures. A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset and interest in the gaming/technology space. Experience working with legal technology tools (e.g. CLM systems, document automation) is advantageous. Interest in leveraging AI and legal technology to improve legal service delivery and efficiency is desirable. 
 If you have the required skills please apply online at searchandselect.com quoting reference number: 16633

Our client seeks a confident Digital Marketing Executive to take the reins of key marketing activity across partner, customer and internal comms for a 12-month fixed term role, helping shape how the business shows up in the market every day. This role is all about turning ideas into impact. From campaigns and content to product launches and partner activity, you'll be right at the centre of making things happen - creating marketing that gets seen, used and talked about. The ideal candidate will have experience in a high-pace, competitive environment, with the passion and drive to deliver multiple projects often to tight deadlines. A creative and strategic thinker, you'll have the energy and drive to go the extra mile and exceed expectations. Working closely with sales, product, design, people experience and senior leaders, you'll take business priorities and turn them into clear, creative and commercially focused marketing across every channel. It's a hands-on role where no two days look the same - one minute you're shaping a campaign, the next you're pulling together a launch, writing content, or bringing a new idea to life. Key Skills and Experience: A marketing or business degree or industry equivalent qualification. Experience delivering multi-channel digital marketing campaigns end-to-end. Experience working across sales, product, and marketing teams. Ability to translate technical/product information into clear messaging.

Notes
An opportunity has arisen for a new team member to join the Unit Pricing team within our Investments Department based at our offices in Royal Court, Castletown.

The Pricing Technician is expected to work independently on routine pricing and valuation activities, seeking guidance from senior colleagues where more complex issues or exceptions arise.

The main responsibilities of the role are:

Validating Guided Architecture pricing activities, including automated and manual price sources and valuations in InvestPro.
Processing and validating policy unit movements and linked external asset trades accurately and on time.
Overseeing Open Architecture price imports and ensuring manual and automated price updates are completed as required.
Monitoring valuation tolerances, investigating discrepancies and coordinating corrective action where required.
Providing first-line support for audit queries and supplying accurate information to support financial reporting.
Supporting quarterly valuation activities for FPIL Open Architecture products.
Identifying issues or anomalies and escalating appropriately to senior colleagues where required.
Helping to maintain accurate unit prices and policy valuations across Guided Architecture and Open Architecture products.

To ensure this role is carried out to the desired level, the successful candidate will need the following skills and experience:

A good standard of education, ideally A-level or equivalent.
A minimum of 3 years' experience working in an Investments department, ideally within a life insurance company.
Familiarity with financial data sources such as Bloomberg and manual price feeds.
Understanding of investment types used in offshore bonds, including mutual funds, ETFs and structured products.
Understanding of Guided Architecture and Open Architecture product structures and how they impact pricing and valuations.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy when processing financial data to strict deadlines.
Competence in Microsoft Excel for data validation and reconciliation.
Ability to identify issues or anomalies and escalate appropriately.
Experience using investment administration systems such as InvestPro, or similar platforms, would be beneficial.
Industry-related qualifications such as CISI, or willingness to study towards them, would be desirable.

We encourage and welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds because we embrace diversity and inclusivity within our business.
If you, or you know someone who is interested in applying for this position, please forward a current CV with a covering letter to careers@ifg-ltd.com 
Closing date for this vacancy will be 24 July 2026.

An opportunity has arisen for a new team member to join the Unit Pricing team within our Investments Department based at our offices in Royal Court, Castletown.

The Pricing Technician is expected to work independently on routine pricing and valuation activities, seeking guidance from senior colleagues where more complex issues or exceptions arise.

The main responsibilities of the role are:

Validating Guided Architecture pricing activities, including automated and manual price sources and valuations in InvestPro.
Processing and validating policy unit movements and linked external asset trades accurately and on time.
Overseeing Open Architecture price imports and ensuring manual and automated price updates are completed as required.
Monitoring valuation tolerances, investigating discrepancies and coordinating corrective action where required.
Providing first-line support for audit queries and supplying accurate information to support financial reporting.
Supporting quarterly valuation activities for FPIL Open Architecture products.
Identifying issues or anomalies and escalating appropriately to senior colleagues where required.
Helping to maintain accurate unit prices and policy valuations across Guided Architecture and Open Architecture products.

To ensure this role is carried out to the desired level, the successful candidate will need the following skills and experience:

A good standard of education, ideally A-level or equivalent.
A minimum of 3 years' experience working in an Investments department, ideally within a life insurance company.
Familiarity with financial data sources such as Bloomberg and manual price feeds.
Understanding of investment types used in offshore bonds, including mutual funds, ETFs and structured products.
Understanding of Guided Architecture and Open Architecture product structures and how they impact pricing and valuations.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy when processing financial data to strict deadlines.
Competence in Microsoft Excel for data validation and reconciliation.
Ability to identify issues or anomalies and escalate appropriately.
Experience using investment administration systems such as InvestPro, or similar platforms, would be beneficial.
Industry-related qualifications such as CISI, or willingness to study towards them, would be desirable.

We encourage and welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds because we embrace diversity and inclusivity within our business.
If you, or you know someone who is interested in applying for this position, please forward a current CV with a covering letter to careers@ifg-ltd.com

Notes
We currently have a number of permanent positions available within the Customer Services AML Team.

Reporting to the AML Manager, the role primarily supports the Company’s AML/CFT defence by undertaking client screening, AML risk assessments and transaction monitoring.  Additionally, the role holder will undertake AML assurance checking and be a point of reference for practical interpretation of AML policies and procedures across the business.

The main duties for the role holder will include:
Support the Company’s AML/CTF defence by undertaking screening and risk assessments of the client base to identify any links to PEPs, sanctions, adverse media and financial crime.
Be a point of reference for practical interpretation of AML policies and procedures across the business.
Work closely with the AML Manager and wider AML team to ensure our AML/CTF obligations are met and will build strong relationships with our Regions and local business areas where required.
Maintain PEP and Higher Risk registers to include preparation of periodic updates and reconciliations.
Investigate results of manual and automated transaction monitoring to ensure SARs are raised accordingly.
Monthly quality assurance checks on agreed processes in respect of compliance with the IFGL AML/CFT internal procedures.
Investigate external fraud incidents and recommend control enhancements where weaknesses have been identified.

To ensure that this role is carried out to the desired level, the successful candidates will need to demonstrate the following skills and experience:
An understanding of the Isle of Man’s regulatory AML framework.
Experience of using screening software such as World-Check, Dow Jones or Moody’s Grid.
Previous employment history within the financial crime function of a regulated financial services company.
Ideally holds an ICA AML qualification and educated to A Level standard.
Must be able to demonstrate practical experience of working on AML remediation projects such as risk rating and obtaining EDD.

If you or you know someone who is interested in applying for this position, please forward a current CV with a covering letter to careers@ifg-ltd.com 

We encourage and welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds because we embrace diversity and inclusivity within our business.

Closing date for this vacancy will be 22 July 2026.

We currently have a permanent position available within the Customer Services AML Team.

Reporting to the AML & Complaints Manager, the role primarily supports the delivery of an AML Remediation project alongside carrying out scheduled reviews for Higher Risk and PEP clients.
The main duties for the role holder will include:
Managing a team of 6-10 AML Analysts primarily identifying and remediating gaps in customer due diligence.
Maintains PEP and Higher Risk Registers ensuring trigger event and scheduled reviews are completed as required.
Works closely with the AML Operations Team Manager and wider AML team to ensure our AML/CTF obligations are met.   
Maintains and builds strong working relationships across the business.
Point of reference for technical queries relating to on-going KYC and EDD matters for personal, corporate and trust clients.
Ensures SARs are raised in response to events such as KYC concerns, adverse media and transaction monitoring.
SME input into business as usual and project support.

To ensure that this role is carried out to the desired level, the successful candidate will need to demonstrate the following skills and experience:
An understanding of the Isle of Man’s AML framework.
Previous worked in a financial crime or new business onboarding role.
Hold an ICA Certificate or Diploma in Anti Money Laundering (or equivalent).
Experience of AML remediation projects.
Performance management including 1:1s, coaching and team development.
Proven ability to delivery projects and tasks on time demonstrating the ability to adapt to changing priorities and resources.

If you or you know someone who is interested in applying for this position, please forward a current CV with a covering letter to careers@ifg-ltd.com 

We encourage and welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds because we embrace diversity and inclusivity within our business.

Notes
An opportunity has arisen for a new team member to join the Unit Pricing team within our Investments Department based at our offices in Royal Court, Castletown.

The Senior Pricing Technician is expected to operate with a higher level of independence, taking ownership of more complex pricing and valuation activities and supporting the wider team with technical guidance.

The main responsibilities of the role are:

Ensuring accurate and timely daily unit pricing, appropriations and policy valuations across Guided Architecture and Open Architecture products.
Validating automated and manual price sources and confirming valuation accuracy in InvestPro.
Executing and reviewing aggregated policy unit movements and external asset trades.
Investigating tolerance breaches and tracking variances, resolving complex exceptions and escalating significant issues where required.
Supporting audit queries, external reporting requirements and risk reporting.
Using Excel and, where required, SQL analysis to support reconciliations and investigations.
Maintaining strong operational controls and helping to mitigate pricing, trading and financial risk.
Completing detailed reviews of large bulk switches and high-value transactions.
Supporting the set-up of new funds in InvestPro and assessing associated operational impacts.

To ensure this role is carried out to the desired level, the successful candidate will need the following skills and experience:

A good standard of education, ideally A-level or equivalent.
Minimum of 5 years’ experience using investment administration systems such as InvestPro.
Strong understanding of fund valuations, contributing factors and anomaly investigation.
Knowledge of trading operations within a life insurance or financial services environment.
High level of accuracy and attention to detail when working with financial data to strict deadlines.
Advanced Excel skills for validation, reconciliation and analysis.
Strong communication skills and the ability to liaise effectively with internal departments and external parties.
Ability to write and interpret SQL code would be beneficial.
Industry-related qualifications, or willingness to study towards them, would be advantageous.
Flexibility to support critical processes outside standard hours at short notice where required.

We encourage and welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds because we embrace diversity and inclusivity within our business.
If you, or you know someone who is interested in applying for this position, please forward a current CV with a covering letter to careers@ifg-ltd.com 
Closing date for this vacancy will be 24 July 2026.

Environment & Regeneration Department – Dilapidation Enforcement Officer.
Grade 6, SCP 24 – 30 (£37,374 – £45,313).

We are seeking a motivated and proactive Dilapidation Enforcement Officer to join our Environment and Regeneration Department and play a key role in helping to maintain and improve the appearance, safety and amenity of the City.

This varied role will involve dealing with dangerous structures, dilapidated and unsightly properties, using a combination of advice, negotiation and enforcement action to ensure buildings and land are brought back to an acceptable condition. You will be a key point of contact for property-related enforcement matters, liaising with owners, members of the public, emergency services, contractors, consultants and other agencies.

The post will also support the Council’s town planning functions, including reviewing planning applications, preparing reports and contributing to the Council’s wider Cleaner, Safer, Greener agenda. The successful candidate will have strong communication and organisational skills, the ability to interpret legislation and technical information, and the confidence to make informed decisions in a busy and varied working environment.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with an interest in property, planning, enforcement or regeneration to make a visible contribution to the City and support improvements that benefit residents, businesses and visitors.

Apply now by heading to our Job Train portal via the Council’s website. For an informal chat about the role please contact Alan Gordon, Community & Enforcement Manager on 696326 or by email at agordon@douglas.gov.im.  Alternatively, you can contact the Human Resources Section on 696455. 

Closing date for submission of applications is Friday 17th July 2026 at 5.00 pm.

Environment & Regeneration Department - City Warden
 
Grade 4, SCP 16 – 22 (£29,731 - £ 35,225)
37-hour week plus contractual overtime (8 hr 10 min weekly). Includes weekend, working 1 in 3.
 
We are looking for a highly motivated individual to take on the role of City Warden.  You will be required to provide excellent customer service to the residents of Douglas, the City centre visitors, users of the Council’s car parks and patrol areas, as directed, on a daily basis.  The role includes improving the experience of Douglas using initiatives and enforcement to deter environmental offences as well as inspecting Council facilities and equipment (e.g., lifebelts, B-lines life-saving equipment) and ensuring care for the environment by carrying out street-scene activities.
 
You must have the ability to resolve conflict in a professional manner, stay calm under pressure, have good communication skills and be able maintain a working knowledge of byelaw enforcement and legislation.  A full clean valid driving licence is essential, and you will be required to work a shift pattern between the hours of 7.00 am and 19:00 pm over a 7-day week (as per the rota), weekend working is 1 in 3.
 
Apply now by heading to our Job Train portal via the Council’s website. For an informal chat about the role please contact Alan Gordon, Community & Enforcement Manager on 696326 or by email at agordon@douglas.gov.im.  Alternatively, you can contact the Human Resources Section on 696455.

**Some of the responsibilities for the Brand Manager position are, but not limited to;**

Engage in the art of following up with both loyal and potential customers, nurturing relationships to bring about further transactions. 
Strive to meet and exceed monthly targets for the sale of both new and used cars. 
Seek out and approach new clients with steadfast determination, arranging meetings to understand and address their needs.

You must possess experience in the sales, a requirement without compromise.
Knowledge of the Kerridge/ADP DMS system a benefit.
The gift of clear communication, both by phone and in person, is essential.
A valid Driving Licence.
Highly presentable, ambitious and target driven, you will have a strong passion for car sales in order to meet and exceed agreed targets for the sale of vehicles and related products.

For more details and to apply contact recruitment@jacksons.je

Notes
At Boots, being an Assistant Manager means creating a team and environment that customers and patients trust — somewhere they feel welcome, looked after and want to come back to. Guided by our purpose, “With You. For Life.”, you’ll play a key role in bringing that to life, supporting your team to deliver care that really makes a difference to customers and colleagues in the moments that matter.

You’ll lead and support your team day to day — setting clear expectations, coaching individuals and helping them grow — while also taking ownership of how things run. From helping a customer find the right solution, to supporting safe and compliant pharmacy services, to driving the standards and results behind the scenes, you’ll be at the heart of it all.

This is a hands-on leadership role where you’ll be balancing people, performance and operations — leading your team, shaping the experience for customers and patients, and taking real ownership of how the store runs and performs. If you're looking for a role that enables you to make a real impact every day, this could be the opportunity for you.

Apply online at Boots.jobs
